races.name: British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Angel Steps
runners_data.comment: Beaten 7 lengths on debut at Wetherby, Angel Steps has plenty to prove in another novice company and ranks last on our figures. The trainer is firing at just 4% over the last fortnight, so there is little in the formbook to encourage.

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.comment: Sprint-bred and stepping forward from a fourth at Ripon last time — where a positive ride showed encouragement — Calef looks capable of better yet to score, and Catterick's sharp track could bring more out of her. The worry is she remains winless and must convert that promise.

runners_data.name: Ma Fille De Reve
runners_data.comment: Pulled too hard and beaten nine lengths on debut at Wetherby, Ma Fille De Reve showed raw speed in her pedigree but must settle much more readily to have a say; hard to fancy until she proves she can control her exuberance.

runners_data.name: Minzelle
runners_data.comment: Third on debut at Haydock after going too hard early and forcing the pace for the closers, Minzelle is a speed-pedigree filly who should benefit from that experience and come into her own dropped to 5f. The trainer's 28% strike rate in recent weeks adds further confidence, though she is yet to score.

runners_data.name: Miss Tuite
runners_data.comment: Showed real ability when second on debut before reverting sharply at Nottingham last time, Miss Tuite clearly has the pace for 5f on good ground and is worth forgiving that reversal — the key risk is whether she can reproduce the promise of her opening outing.

runners_data.name: Roots In Touche
runners_data.comment: Beaten only a length and a quarter when runner-up at Beverley on her only start, Roots In Touche showed good early zip and ought to take a forward step with that experience under her belt. She handles today's distance and going and is a clear danger yet to score.

runners_data.name: Sable Noir
runners_data.comment: A Blackbeard filly foaled in late March and a half-sister to 5f performer Merpati Sejoli, Sable Noir is bred to be quick and the yard has a strong record with first-timers — betting market signals from the wide draw will be worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Warby
runners_data.comment: By high-class sprinter Ardad and a half-sister to smart 5f performer Society Kiss, Warby fetched 62,000 guineas as a yearling and is trained by a top Catterick handler — betting moves on debut will be the tell.

races.name: Jimmy Loxam Is 80 Today "Confined" Handicap (For horses Which Have Not Won In 2026 Flat Turf Season)

runners_data.name: Wen Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two recent placings over 5f in Good ground; Cam Hardie is a positive booking and 19 days since last run suggests a fresh, well-timed entry, though sim-going record shows modest win-rate.|
runners_data.comment: Placed at Carlisle and Ripon in recent starts and effective at 5f on any going, Wen Moon ran to form when beaten two lengths off this exact mark at Ripon last time and looks set to run her race again from the same weight.

runners_data.name: Storm Call
runners_data.note: Won over 5f in Good conditions two runs back for Michael & David Easterby, and the 90-day break may be deliberate freshening — Joanna Mason takes the ride and the course-distance form is the most relevant item in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Off the track for three months and below par when last seen fifth at Wolverhampton, Storm Call is an inconsistent type who is fitted with first-time headgear today — effective at 5-6f on a sound surface but needs to show his best after a lengthy break.

runners_data.name: Polka
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 5f on Standard going with headgear (hood) fitted, and returns after a 128-day absence; a natural hold-up runner who will need to cover extra ground given the redistribution in this back-heavy field — the style-fit discount applies.|
runners_data.comment: Back after a 128-day absence and ranked bottom on our figures, Polka benefited from a stiff track when landing a maiden at Newcastle last time and her tendency to pull hard makes her unpredictable returning to handicap company despite that confidence-boosting success.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f performer with the most relevant recent form in similar conditions, placing in three of his last five; was back out only 12 days ago so fitness is not a concern, and Adrian Nicholls has had three winners from nine runners in the 14-day window — but genuine hold-up preference means he is further forward than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent at 5f on good to soft and quick ground and operating at just 1lb above her last winning mark, Tees Aggregates arrives with a trainer in strong form and races from a familiar draw — winless in recent starts but the profile and current mark both point to a big run.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, able to set its own uncontested fractions; tongue-tie fitted, Simon Gray in the saddle, and the trainer has three winners from 13 runners in the past fortnight — limited sim-going wins (0 from 3 relevant) is a note of caution despite the tactical advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent, Our Absent Friends went a touch too freely and was beaten three and a quarter lengths off a mark 2lb higher than today's at Ripon last time — settle better here and she is a live danger over this distance on any going, yet to score.

runners_data.name: Woodhay Whisper
runners_data.note: Hood fitted and a natural hold-up runner, but recent form figures make bleak reading with no wins or places from five in similar going; Ron Barr has just one winner from two runners in the 14-day window, and being forced off its preferred backmarker position compresses the already thin chance further.|
runners_data.comment: First-time hood on today and back on a winning mark, Woodhay Whisper probably needed the run at Thirsk last time when beaten four and a half lengths — but recent efforts have been poor and a sharper performance is required to get back in contention.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Placed twice at this trip in Good-ground conditions and runs just six days after its last start, so Tim Easterby clearly thinks the horse is in a good place; blinkers fitted, veteran at eight, and while it carries the lowest weight, the blinker-plus-hold-up profile means it needs a truly run race to land a blow.|
runners_data.comment: Showing signs of better of late and effective at 5f on today's going, Albegone has a top Catterick trainer handling the booking — yet to score in recent starts but the fresh angle of first-time blinkers and a fair mark make him a genuine each-way player.

races.paceDynamic: Our Absent Friends is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 5f handicap at Catterick and, with no genuine rival to push it off the front, should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a pressured burn. The going is Good to Firm, which suits a fleet-footed front-runner dictating its own fractions on a straight five-furlong track where the rail draw and an early stride advantage carry real weight. However, this field is stacked with hold-up horses — Polka, Tees Aggregates, Woodhay Whisper and Albegone are all natural hold-up types who cannot all occupy the rear; several will be forced wider or closer to the pace than their preferred position, meaning the shape benefits runners who can adapt to a mid-race slot rather than those relying on a pure late charge from the back. This race shape strongly favours the front-running profile of Our Absent Friends and any prominent-to-midfield runners that can travel within striking range of a modest, uncontested gallop, rather than horses requiring a strong pace to deliver their finish from well off the bridle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends gets a clean break and sets its own uncontested fractions, dictating throughout on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: If Our Absent Friends gets a clean break and sets its own uncontested fractions, dictating throughout on Good to Firm ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collide
scenarios.trigger: If a horse from the chasing group travels strongly enough to press Our Absent Friends in the final two furlongs, turning it into a two-horse sprint.
scenarios.body: If a horse from the chasing group travels strongly enough to press Our Absent Friends in the final two furlongs, turning it into a two-horse sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested pace proves artificially slow and the field bunches, allowing a true hold-up runner to produce a late run down the centre of the track.
scenarios.body: If the uncontested pace proves artificially slow and the field bunches, allowing a true hold-up runner to produce a late run down the centre of the track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Off Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and multiple horses simultaneously make their move at the two-furlong pole, creating a scrambling finish with no clear winner emerging from any single zone.
scenarios.body: If the field crawls early and multiple horses simultaneously make their move at the two-furlong pole, creating a scrambling finish with no clear winner emerging from any single zone.

watchPoints.text: Our Absent Friends is the only horse who will get its natural running position — watch the gate break, because if it misses the kick and gets swallowed up, the entire pace map dissolves.|

Storm Call is the key danger to a controlled leader: watch whether Joanna Mason presses forward in the early strides after 90 days off, because a fresher-than-expected horse making its move from the two-furlong pole is the most likely disruption to Scenario A.|

Polka returns from 128 days and wore a hood last time when winning — check whether headgear is retained on raceday, as any reported equipment change would significantly alter its chance given the redistribution penalty already applied.|

With four horses all naturally wanting to come from the rear, watch the first furlong for crowding and checking — any horse that loses two lengths at the start in this flat 5f sprint will find the deficit very hard to recover against an uncontested leader.|

Tees Aggregates is the most exposed hold-up horse in the field with five recent 5f runs at similar going levels; if it is seen travelling smoothly just off midfield in the first half of the race, it becomes the most credible late threat despite the style-fit caution.|

races.name: Catterick Racecourse Supporting Racing Staff Week Handicap

runners_data.name: Thehunnebelllegacy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has placed twice at 6f on soft/standard but has yet to show similar form on good ground, recording just one placed finish from nine runs in similar conditions — the quick surface is a legitimate query, and Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim helps the weight burden but cannot compensate if the pace is too slow to suit.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without threatening over 6-7f, Thehunnebelllegacy was beaten only three lengths off a higher mark back here last time and is respected back down in trip — though our figures leave him a fair bit to find to take a hand.

runners_data.name: Elashgar
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on standard ground and placed twice at this trip; she is the lone pace-maker here and that is a powerful tactical position on good-to-firm Catterick — Conor Whiteley's 7lb claim means she carries a competitive weight, and the 57-day absence is the only flag against a potentially commanding showing.
runners_data.comment: A likeable sort who landed a success over 6f on the all-weather earlier this term and was usually consistent prior to that, Elashgar was out of sorts on turf at Nottingham last time — the question is whether he brings his all-weather form across to today's going.

runners_data.name: Rivera Queen
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer who has placed on good ground but is a true rear-runner reassigned closer on the map due to the glut of hold-up types — Clifford Lee rides for a yard firing at 25%, and the tongue-tie is noted, but the redistribution means she may not get the late run she needs if the tempo is modest.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye finishing strongly from a hopeless position on her handicap debut at Brighton — where first-time headgear was worn and she was given too much to do — Rivera Queen looks on a generous mark based on that debut evidence and a trainer in form strengthens the case, yet to score.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Wears a hood today for Daragh Bourke's small but active yard after finishing fourth on good ground last time; she has shown enough over 6f to suggest the trip is fine, though her seven-furlong efforts on standard ground haven't encouraged confidence that she has the pace for a sharp track like Catterick.
runners_data.comment: Blocked out of things from the off and never in contention when comfortably held back here last time, Saxon Grace is down to a competitive mark but has yet to score in recent starts and looks an exposed maiden — first-time cheekpieces offer a modest angle for improvement.

runners_data.name: Our Hero Matty
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh partners a horse whose best recent effort was a third at 6f on standard ground, but who has finished seventh or worse in five of his last six starts — a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping by field composition, and the trainer's cold 14-day strike-rate (0/2) offers no compensating angle.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Newcastle last time out and out of the frame in each of his last two starts, Our Hero Matty is inconsistent and ranks last on our figures — form goes in and out and a sizeable revival is needed.

runners_data.name: Long Shot
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's gelding has placed twice at 7f on good ground and ran respectably over 6f at Goodwood; wears a hood and handles good ground, making this going tick, but he is a true hold-up horse repositioned by the field's pace shape — David Allan's experience could help him find a route through if the race develops.
runners_data.comment: Beaten only three lengths off this mark at Redcar when racing too keenly at the head of affairs under first-time blinkers, Long Shot drops back in trip today with first-time cheekpieces — better efforts over 6-7f and a top Catterick trainer make him a genuine threat, winless in recent starts notwithstanding.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over on a filly who has placed in four of her last six starts and goes well on good ground at 6f — the form book shows clear consistency and good ground suits her, but she is a hold-up type re-mapped by the density of closers in this field and needs the pace to be stronger than Elashgar is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Three successive runner-up finishes including off this very mark at Carlisle last time — beaten only three quarters of a length — show Battenburg Belle is in consistent form at 6f on today's going; a cold trainer strike rate is the one reservation for a mare who keeps finding one too good.

races.paceDynamic: Elashgar is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Catterick, and with no genuine pace rival to press her, she can dictate a controlled, measured tempo from the outset. The remainder of the field — Thehunnebelllegacy, Rivera Queen, Saxon Grace, Our Hero Matty, Long Shot, and Battenburg Belle — are all hold-up types, meaning the pace is thin and unlikely to be truly pressured. This field holds considerably more true hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Rivera Queen, Our Hero Matty, Long Shot, and Battenburg Belle are the most likely to find themselves racing closer than their natural style, with Elashgar and Saxon Grace (in her headgear) the most plausible to secure prominent ground. With a single pace-setter controlling a modest tempo on quick ground, this race shape strongly favours Elashgar to steal and hold a lead she is not being asked to fight for — a wire-to-wire scenario is the dominant probability, with closers needing the pace to be honest enough to reel her in late, which is far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Elashgar Leads, Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Elashgar breaks cleanly and is allowed to set her own pace unchallenged through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Elashgar breaks cleanly and is allowed to set her own pace unchallenged through the first two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Swamp Late Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Elashgar sets a marginally stronger gallop than expected or ties up in the final furlong, allowing the closers to arrive in time.
scenarios.body: If Elashgar sets a marginally stronger gallop than expected or ties up in the final furlong, allowing the closers to arrive in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If Elashgar is checked or hampered and the pace collapses entirely, creating a messy race with no true flow.
scenarios.body: If Elashgar is checked or hampered and the pace collapses entirely, creating a messy race with no true flow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Front Runner Fades Late
scenarios.trigger: If Elashgar is tackled wider than expected by a rival adopting more aggressive tactics, burning energy too early.
scenarios.body: If Elashgar is tackled wider than expected by a rival adopting more aggressive tactics, burning energy too early.

watchPoints.text: Elashgar jumping cleanly from the stalls is critical — if she misses the break, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes a muddling contest with no true leader.

Battenburg Belle's recent placing run (2nd, 2nd, 2nd in three recent starts) makes her the most consistent finisher in the field — watch whether Cieren Fallon positions her closer than expected given how slow the pace may be.

Long Shot's hood application and Easterby's tactical nous via David Allan means he could be ridden more prominently than his natural style suggests — if he pushes forward, he becomes an unexpected pace factor.

With five of the seven runners being genuine hold-up types, the early furlongs are likely to feature a bunched, slowly-strung field behind Elashgar — watch for crowding and potential interference on the bend as redistributed closers find themselves in unfamiliar racing positions.

Good-to-firm ground confirmed for this race favours quick-actioned, prominent types over heavy-ground closers — Saxon Grace's hood and Rivera Queen's tongue-tie are both headgear angles worth tracking if either finishes closer than market expectation suggests.

races.name: Congratulations To The Happy Couple EBF Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Diamont Katie
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose recent 1W4P record at similar going and back-to-back placed runs over 7f show clear aptitude for the trip; runs off a career-high OR and is racing out of a fully front-running role mapped as prominent, which slightly tempers confidence she'll dominate at this mark.
runners_data.comment: Finished third beaten two and a quarter lengths off 74 last time despite being given too much to do, Diamont Katie landed a wide-margin success at Pontefract three starts back following a wind operation and remains competitive at 6-7f on today's ground — 1lb higher here but in the mix.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form at Southwell over 1m last time out but all her best efforts have come over that distance or further; stepping back to 7f on ground faster than she typically encounters is the primary concern for this natural hold-up mare.
runners_data.comment: Landed a success off a lower mark at Southwell penultimate start but below form in eighth off 74 last time, Alessia Fernanda is in and out of form at 7-9f on most going — first-time tongue-tie adds an unknown dimension and she may have more to offer if it helps her settle.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Queen
runners_data.note: Holds a 7f course win at Catterick and a strong second at the track which makes her the most credible hold-up threat, though her recent run of 7th and 8th finishes on good suggests she needs things to fall perfectly her way in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Keen early and dropping away when beaten more than eight lengths at Carlisle last time, Ziggy's Queen is better than that effort suggests and is effective at 6f on most going — the mark looks a shade high until she proves she can keep the lid on her enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a strong jockey booking and the horse clearly has ability, but her true style is to race right at the back and she has been placed further forward on this map due to the density of hold-up horses in the field — her last three runs all produced single-figure finishes in similar scenarios.
runners_data.comment: Below form in each of her last four starts and beaten nine lengths at Beverley last time, In A Hurry is yet to score in recent starts and is hard to support at present — a first-time tongue-tie is fitted today and better trips of 7f on a sound surface are in her favour if the headgear helps.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's filly has been remarkably consistent with two seconds from two starts over 7f on good ground this year, and her prominent style maps perfectly to what this race shape demands; the trainer has a quiet 14-day record but this form profile is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back placed finishes including a half-length second off a mark 3lb higher than today's at Musselburgh put Homestrait right in the picture, effective at 6-7f on today's going — yet to score but first-time cheekpieces could sharpen her further and she is a clear danger.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner who has won twice on good going over 7f and brings a recent run just seven days ago; her prominent style suits the anticipated race shape and her light weight of 127lbs is an additional factor worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Landed two wins in recent starts, including over course and distance, before a flat effort last time when pushed into the lead too soon, Velvet Rhythm is effective at 6-7f on a sound surface and returns at the same mark — that latest blot can be forgiven with a more patient ride.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Queen
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's filly is a genuine hold-up horse displaced into a midfield position on this map due to the overcrowding of rear-dwellers; her best recent effort was a third on good over 7f which is relevant, but racing out of her natural role reduces her prospects materially.
runners_data.comment: Ran close to her best at Musselburgh last time — where she finished only a length and a half behind the leaders off a mark just 1lb lower — Yorkshire Queen is lightly exposed at 7f and capable of further progress; inconsistent this term but that latest effort confirmed she retains ability, yet to score.

races.paceDynamic: Diamont Katie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Catterick's flat seven furlongs on good-to-firm ground. Homestrait and Velvet Rhythm will look to press from prominent positions just behind, meaning a small group of three horses could dominate the early framing while the remainder settle in behind. The hold-up contingent — Alessia Fernanda, Ziggy's Queen, In A Hurry, and Yorkshire Queen — will be hunting a pace that may never become truly testing enough to bring them into play from the rear. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track a controlled tempo and pick off a front-runner who hasn't been pressured; the field carries more hold-up horses than can be accommodated naturally, and In A Hurry and Yorkshire Queen are the runners most likely displaced from their preferred positions, reducing their realistic winning chances.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Diamont Katie leads at a fair clip and Homestrait or Velvet Rhythm track closely throughout, the race unfolds as a test of stamina from the front.
scenarios.body: If Diamont Katie leads at a fair clip and Homestrait or Velvet Rhythm track closely throughout, the race unfolds as a test of stamina from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do, Diamont Katie keeps the lead all the way.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely modest and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do, Diamont Katie keeps the lead all the way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Rattles Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and open a gap for a finisher, a hold-up horse can close late.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and open a gap for a finisher, a hold-up horse can close late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Diamont Katie goes too steady and the race turns into a sprint finish from halfway, midfield scramblers benefit in a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: If Diamont Katie goes too steady and the race turns into a sprint finish from halfway, midfield scramblers benefit in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Homestrait has produced two placed efforts over 7f on good ground this season in a prominent style that maps directly to the dominant race shape — she is the primary danger to Diamont Katie if the front-runner is tracked throughout.

Velvet Rhythm's light weight and recent winning form on good ground over 7f make her worth monitoring from a prominent position, particularly if she travels strongly into the final two furlongs under Rowan Scott.
Diamont Katie sets the entire pace tempo — if she goes unusually slowly, the shape collapses and hold-up horses gain an unexpected chance; watch her early sectionals carefully.

In A Hurry and Yorkshire Queen are both natural rear-dwellers mapped forward in this analysis due to redistribution — if either drifts back to their instinctive position at the start, their chances decrease further unless the pace is genuinely searching.
Ziggy's Queen's Catterick course form over 7f is the strongest historical angle among the hold-up horses — if any closer is to land a blow, she is the one with the track profile to do it.

races.name: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Handicap

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up performer for Martin Todhunter and David Nolan with ten runs on similar going yielding one win and four places; 22 days since last run looks routine, and the 16f trip suits, but the recent string of 6-0-3-6 gives little confidence of a career revival at OR 70.
runners_data.comment: Effective over staying trips on most ground, Arrange briefly threatened before fading into sixth at Thirsk last time and may not be what she was — but with a much-reduced mark in a small field, a return to better form cannot be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old arrives on the back of a win over this course and distance on Good ground (1 from 3 on similar going) and carries the significant tactical asset of being the field's sole front-runner; a trainer strike rate of 14 from 112 over 14 days is modest but the race shape does the heavy lifting here — David Allan simply needs to control the fractions.
runners_data.comment: Progressive over staying trips, Treasure Islands landed a success off a lower mark earlier in recent starts and has run creditably in defeat since, finishing third off this very mark in a stronger race last time. Unexposed at staying distances and with a top record at this course, the opportunity looks well timed.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up mare trained by Samantha & Jacqueline Coward who finished second over 12f on Good most recently; Joanna Mason takes the ride, but eight wins from 15 on similar going have all come in place positions (0W4P) and she will need a pace collapse rather than a steady leader to get her head in front.
runners_data.comment: Looked the likely winner at Thirsk last time before being worn down close home, beaten only three quarters of a length off a mark 1lb lower than today's, Valley Of Flowers is a consistent stayer on any going — enthusiasm questions remain but the ability to go very close is clearly there.

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — its two placed efforts in 10 similar-going runs came from the rear — but the 36-day absence, a form string reading 6-4-6-7-0, and the STYLE_FIT flag for effectively racing out of its preferred deep hold-up position all weigh against it; Jack Nicholls' 5lb claim offers marginal compensation.
runners_data.comment: Pushed too prominently in front and beaten at Ripon last time, Twilight Safari is yet to score in either code and is better suited to ten furlongs — needs a significant step up to play a role here.

races.paceDynamic: Treasure Islands is the lone confirmed front-runner in this small four-runner field over two miles at Catterick on Good to Firm ground, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, David Allan's mount should be able to dictate at a comfortable, controlled tempo from the outset. The three hold-up types — Arrange, Valley Of Flowers, and Twilight Safari — will all be racing from off the pace, meaning there is no genuine pace pressure to unsettle Treasure Islands and the fractions are likely to be modest through the early and middle stages. Twilight Safari is a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more rear-tracking types than genuine slots at the back, but its natural instinct is to race last or close to it, not in midfield. This race shape strongly favours a horse capable of making all or racing prominently, as the lack of early tempo will compress the race into a late dash and front-runners or prominent racers who have conserved energy under a generous lead will hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Treasure Islands Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Treasure Islands jumps cleanly and is allowed to set a gentle, uncontested gallop throughout the two miles.
scenarios.body: If Treasure Islands jumps cleanly and is allowed to set a gentle, uncontested gallop throughout the two miles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunches The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so compressed that all four runners effectively race in a tight pack and the race becomes a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is so compressed that all four runners effectively race in a tight pack and the race becomes a sprint finish from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Treasure Islands goes too fast too soon and the hold-up runners are able to pick them off in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Treasure Islands goes too fast too soon and the hold-up runners are able to pick them off in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Backmarker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fast and Treasure Islands ties up inside the final quarter mile, leaving the field in disarray.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely fast and Treasure Islands ties up inside the final quarter mile, leaving the field in disarray.

watchPoints.text: Watch Treasure Islands' early behaviour at the start — if David Allan gets a clean break and immediately slots in front uncontested, the race is effectively over as a tactical contest.

Monitor the pace at the halfway point: if the field is bunched and Treasure Islands has not stretched clear, Valley Of Flowers and Arrange will both be travelling and a competitive finish becomes more likely.

Twilight Safari's true running style is deep hold-up, but the small field may force Jack Nicholls to take closer order than he would like — watch whether it settles in a genuinely restrained position or ends up racing within a length of the leaders against its nature.

With only four runners, any significant incident — a stumble, a horse hanging — will have an outsized effect on the result given the compressed field and modest pace; Arrange's age (8) and recent below-par efforts at 16f are worth monitoring in running.

Catterick's 2m trip is confirmed Good to Firm per the going report — note that all three hold-up horses have at least some form on similar ground, so the surface alone does not create a meaningful differentiator between them.

races.name: Racing Again 8th July Handicap

runners_data.name: Sanditon
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with five consecutive 7f runs at Catterick's standard trip, trained by Charlie Johnston whose yard is 5/48 in the last 14 days; consistent placed effort last time but needs the pace to be strong enough to get competitive, which this shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Back to form when landing a classified event at Wolverhampton by three lengths last time, Sanditon is effective at 7f on a sound surface and has to be respected returned to handicap company — the test is whether that revival holds up against regular handicappers.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old is the race's pace-maker and carries the structural advantage of Catterick's tight 7f uncontested; only 6 days since last run and 2/2 placed finishes over today's 7f on similar good ground make this the pivotal runner in how the race is shaped.
runners_data.comment: A course-and-distance winner off a higher mark who had been running back into form until pulling hard and dropping away tamely at Beverley last time, Emerald Army is effective at 6-7f on today's going — a cold trainer at 4% and a wide draw are added concerns for a winless run.

runners_data.name: Captain Cess
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two recent placed efforts over 6f on good ground, stepping up to 7f at Catterick for Declan Carroll; 7 days since last run and a poor record beyond 6f on softer ground, but the quick surface here suits and he can close from just off the pace if tracking sensibly.
runners_data.comment: Caught in traffic at a key point when beaten a length off this very mark at Wetherby last time, Captain Cess is unexposed at 7f and has handled today's going — a clear run here could make all the difference for a horse who retains latent ability, yet to score.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type with one win and four places from six runs on good ground and a solid recent form string of 331324; David Nolan's use of 5f-dominant tracks in recent outings raises a slight question over this 7f, but the going is right and the consistency is notable.
runners_data.comment: Landed a neck success at Hamilton earlier in recent starts and ran to form when fourth off a mark 1lb higher last time, Classy Clarets is consistent at 5-7f on a sound surface — the mark looks a shade stiff but first-time headgear could provide a sharpening effect.

runners_data.name: War Memorial
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's five-year-old is a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield mapping because of the field's composition — his best Catterick effort came over 7f on good ground (a win) and the 7lb claimer Conor Whiteley rides, though the STYLE_FIT discount and trainer's cold 0/4 in 14 days tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Back on song when third beaten only half a length off this exact mark last time, staying the longer trip well, War Memorial landed a neck success at Musselburgh three starts back and is generally in good form — effective at 7f and could handle the mile if the going suits.

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer who is the most likely horse to test Emerald Army for the lead; record shows 1 win and 5 places from recent 6-7f starts on similar going, and John David Riches has no recent winners but this horse is consistent enough to frame.
runners_data.comment: In good form prior to being hampered and not picking up when it mattered at Carlisle last time, Rain Cap is effective at 6-7f and capable of going well when there is a proper pace to aim at — first-time visor is a fresh angle and the mark is fair, though yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Blue Jay Way
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose mapping to midfield reflects the overcrowded rear of this field rather than his natural style; best effort (a 7f win on Standard ground) came from off the pace and the 0/3 trainer record in 14 days offers no support, while the STYLE_FIT flag is a structural concern.
runners_data.comment: Below form when dropped in trip at Wolverhampton last time, Blue Jay Way has been in better form over 6-7f and is fitted with first-time cheekpieces for this return to a more suitable distance — inconsistent but not without ability on a workable mark.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old is a hold-up type reassigned to midfield in the mapping; a modest form string of 60-066 and a preference for 8-9f trips makes today's 7f on quick ground look short, and 32 days off adds a fitness query — little to recommend on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: In poor form over recent starts and comfortably held at Musselburgh last time, Misemerald is effective at 7-8f on today's going but the stronger rivals in this field look to hold the edge, and she is yet to score.

runners_data.name: Martin's Brig
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who naturally races at the rear but is mapped to midfield due to field congestion; best recent effort was a 7f good-ground placing but a form line of 8-9876 and blinkered headgear suggest a hold on his ability — the STYLE_FIT discount and flat 0/6 trainer strike rate compound the negatives.
runners_data.comment: Out of form over recent starts and below par back on turf at Redcar last time, Martin's Brig is effective at 7-8f and the first-time blinkers add a small wildcard — hard to make a case until the form shows signs of life.

runners_data.name: Wath Court
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's six-year-old carries a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag, has been mapped to midfield rather than his natural rearward position, and comes into this race just 2 days after his last run; a form string of 900600 and a record of 0 wins and 0 places from six comparable-going runs makes this the most structurally exposed runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Hamilton only two days ago and with largely poor form in recent starts, Wath Court ranks last on our figures by some distance — the combination of tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time today is a final roll of the dice.

races.paceDynamic: Emerald Army is the one confirmed front-runner in this 7f Catterick handicap and, with no genuine rival to press for the lead, James Sullivan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground. Rain Cap is the only other horse with prominent tendencies, giving Emerald Army a largely uncontested lead and the ability to control tempo from the front. The remainder of the field — Sanditon, Captain Cess, Classy Clarets, War Memorial, Blue Jay Way, Misemerald, Martin's Brig and Wath Court — are all natural hold-up or midfield types, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring them into the race off a truly searching gallop. Several runners tagged as redistributed (War Memorial, Blue Jay Way, Misemerald, Martin's Brig, Wath Court) are genuine hold-up horses who cannot all find their natural position at the rear and will be shuffled into midfield; of these, War Memorial and Blue Jay Way are most likely to actually secure a forward berth given their profiles. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a horse that can track close to the controlled pace and quicken from a prominent or just-off-the-pace position — a lone front-runner dictating on quick ground at Catterick's tight 7f is a potent tactical advantage that makes sit-and-sprint hold-up raiders structurally disadvantaged.

watchPoints.text: Emerald Army sets off in front — if Sullivan is allowed a clear lead into the first bend at Catterick, the race may effectively be over by halfway; watch whether Rain Cap (Tindall) fires from the stalls to challenge for the lead and whether that duel materialises.

War Memorial's redistribution is the key X-factor — if Conor Whiteley elects to push forward early rather than settle mid-pack, it could inject pace into the race and completely alter the tempo dynamic, opening the race up for hold-up horses like Sanditon and Classy Clarets.

Wath Court's two-day turnaround combined with a fade-in-finish flag and zero wins or places on comparable going makes it a horse to avoid in any scenario — but watch whether its prominent early position (if taken) compresses the pace in the first few furlongs.

Classy Clarets' recent form (three consecutive placed efforts) is the most consistent in the field outside Emerald Army — if the pace is even marginally stronger than expected in Scenario B, David Nolan's ability to position from a hold-up role makes this the main beneficiary to monitor on the home turn.

Blue Jay Way won over this exact 7f trip at Catterick on Standard ground — though today is Good to Firm and the STYLE_FIT flag applies, Mikkel Mortensen's handling of where this horse ends up in the first two furlongs is worth tracking as a signal of how genuine the field's pace truly is.
